newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SAS sees 8-10 pct passenger growth in Russia.
newsitem.headline: SAS sees 8-10 pct passenger growth in Russia.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) sees Russian international passenger and air cargo traffic growing steadily over the next few years, SAS's general manager in Moscow said on Wednesday.
Gunther Sollinger told a news conference Russian international passenger traffic would rise 8-10 percent annually over the next few years, against 4-5 percent in Western Europe.

He said Russian airlines Aeroflot, Transaero and a few others carriers would soon compete with Western carriers on international routes but said they needed to work closer with foreign carriers to integrate international services.
Sollinger said SAS carried about 130,000 passengers between Scandinavian countries and Russia in 1996, an 8-10 percent rise on 1995.

SAS passenger traffic between Stockholm and the northern European Russian city Arkhangelsk, which began last September, had been low, he said. "But we think this region will be developed...and it will become promising."
Currently, SAS operates regular flights between Stockholm and Moscow (14 flights a week), St Petersburg (11 flights) and Kaliningrad (four flights).
Sollinger said SAS did not plan to open any new destination in Russia this year.
